thread:
incident-bot: [ALERT] Elevated 502/timeout rate observed for customer StratusGrid (stratusgrid-prod) in privnet-us-east-1. NLB 'stratusgrid-nlb' showing 18% 502s, spike started ~10:58 UTC. Affected: dedicated pool tenant-dpool-7 (ingress + egress). Pager: @raj. Runbook: https://redwood.runbooks/privnet-nlb

raj (oncall): On it. Pulling NLB target health and recent deploys. Can someone confirm customer impact? @emily

emily (cs): Customer reports UI timeouts and batch job failures since ~10:55. Error payloads show connection resets and 502s from edge. They say some requests succeed intermittently. They're on a tight SLA right now.

tom (eng-infra): I see a config change rolled at 10:50 in the infra pipeline: security-group hardening for privnet VPC. Ops bot flagged it as a partial rollback candidate. Quick check: inbound rules now explicitly deny ephemeral-range for non-whitelisted sources — could be breaking NLB client->backend flows which rely on ephemeral ports for egress.

ops-bot: [deploy-bot] rollout "privnet-sg-hardening" matched target VPC: vpc-0a1b2c3d (stratusgrid). Status: COMPLETED @ 10:50 (sha: b7e9f2). Automated guardrail match: CUSTOMER_VPC_LABEL -> true.

raj (oncall): If SG blocked ephemeral source ports we can see established connections reset. I'm going to rollback that SG change for the stratusgrid VPC only, then validate. Initiating scoped rollback now.

tom (eng-infra): Logging some checks — NLB target-group health: 3/6 healthy intermittently. Sample commands I ran from bastion:
```
# check target health
aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:...:targetgroup/stratus-tg

# ssh to node and curl backend
ssh -i ~/.ssh/bastion ubuntu@10.240.5.12 "curl -v http://10.240.1.12:8080/health"
```
Output: a few timeouts followed by HTTP/1.1 200. Pattern looks like connection collisions.

ops-bot: rollback action triggered: revert security group change for vpc-0a1b2c3d -> applying previous SG ruleset (change-id c0ffee).

raj (oncall): Rollback applied. Next step: flush conntrack entries for the tenant CIDR on NAT and nodes — stale conntrack can keep resets after SG change. Tom, can you run the conntrack flush for 10.2.3.0/24?

tom (eng-infra): Running:
```
sudo conntrack -D -s 10.2.3.0/24 || true
sudo conntrack -D -d 10.2.3.0/24 || true
```
Also observed a high number of TIME_WAIT and CLOSE_WAIT entries for that CIDR before flush.

raj (oncall): Flushed conntrack on NAT gateways and affected nodes. Re-registering NLB targets to push new connections.

ops-bot: [action] deregistering targets from target-group stratus-tg -> waiting 10s -> re-registering to force new TCP handshakes.

emily (cs): Customer reports partial improvement: about 60% of previously failing requests are now succeeding (they see retries ok). Still seeing occasional spikes.

raj (oncall): Shifting small percentage of traffic to secondary dedicated pool (dpool-8) as canary while we observe. 30% traffic shift in-flight.

tom (eng-infra): Monitoring metrics: 502 rate falling from 18% -> 4% over 8 minutes after rollback + conntrack flush + target re-register. NLB connection reset metric decreased.

jennifer (senior-oncall): Thanks team. Good mitigation path. Keep the traffic shift for 20 more minutes, then gradually move back if stable. Log the deploy pipeline entry that allowed SG change to cross-customer VPCs — we need a guardrail.

raj (oncall): Will keep monitoring. Current status: degraded -> partial service. Customer impact reduced to intermittent failures; no data loss. On-call will remain on this thread until fully green. ETA re-evaluate 11:25 UTC.

ops-bot: [monitoring] 11:14 UTC summary: 502 rate 3.8%, error budget consumption reduced. Canary pool dpool-8 healthy.

emily (cs): Customer confirms end-to-end jobs are completing again, small retries required. They're ok with our mitigations but request root cause and ETA for full resolution.

raj (oncall): Short-term mitigation complete: rolled back SG change for customer VPC, flushed conntrack, re-registered targets, shifted canary traffic. Next: full rollback audit + postmortem. Actions:
- infra: add tenant-tagging gate to SG hardening rollout pipeline (tom)
- infra: add automated preflight check that ensures ephemeral port allowances for NLB-backed tenant VPCs (tom)
- devex: add quick test in deploy job to simulate backend handshake (raj/devex)
- cs: follow-up with customer and schedule joint incident review (emily)

jennifer (senior-oncall): Adding one more follow-up: create a runbook step to explicitly check for deploys touching SGs in the last 30 minutes during incident triage. Also assign priority for the infra fix. :thumbsup:

raj (oncall): Acknowledged. Moving to watch mode. If we stay <1% 502s for 20m we'll close this thread. Thanks all.

ops-bot: [incident-note] Mitigation applied: scoped SG rollback + conntrack flush + target re-registration + 30% traffic canary shift. Current state: stabilizing. Recommended follow-ups assigned.
